claims.text: Cloud Manager rolling changes can stall when DNS or firewall problems prevent the MongoDB Agent from inspecting other members. Check inter-member reachability and agent access to cloud.mongodb.com over HTTPS before treating an In Progress deployment as a database defect. (low confidence)

Ops Manager 8.0.20 release notes document a fix for job workers stuck waiting on a data-fetch lock that stopped scheduled-job progress. When jobs stop advancing, check the installed patch level as well as configuration and resource health. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-19)

Cloud Manager troubleshooting requires SAN-bearing TLS certificates for MongoDB Agents built with Go versions that no longer permit hostname validation through CommonName alone. Check certificate names when agent upgrades expose TLS failures. (low confidence)

Insufficient disk capacity can break backups or restores. A standalone backup blockstore can go offline when full; restoring compressed snapshots also requires space for both the archive and extracted database files. (medium confidence)

TLS errors can block different control paths: an Ops Manager operator user reported an agent hostname/certificate mismatch, while another reported application startup failure caused by an untrusted certificate chain. Cloud Manager documents the requirement for SAN-bearing certificates. Check hostname coverage and CA trust on each connection. (medium confidence)

Automated restore can fail when source and target storage settings differ, including storage.engine, storage.directoryPerDB, WiredTiger block compression, or directoryForIndexes. Ops Manager reports mismatches after the attempt; correct target settings before retrying. (high confidence)

For recovery of Ops Manager itself, backing up database data without the original gen.key leaves a startup/decryption failure. The recovery guide also warns that starting Ops Manager before restoring its backing databases can create inconsistent state. (low confidence)

Online automation-config encryption adds a KMIP dependency. If an agent cannot decrypt its local backup and cannot reach Ops Manager, it enters an error state and retries. Hardware or agent-version changes can invalidate local artifacts, but reachable Ops Manager can supply fresh configuration automatically. (low confidence)

Historical operator defects can resemble configuration errors: Enterprise Kubernetes Operator 1.14.0 fixed failure to mount a custom CA into the Backup Daemon in hybrid mode, and 1.18.0 fixed a liveness probe that could report healthy after the automation agent died. These are documented fixes, not evidence that current versions retain those bugs. (low confidence)

DNS or firewall failures between MongoDB processes can prevent automation from determining peer state and completing a rolling change. Backup agents can likewise fail when replica-set connectivity or authentication fails. Test from the affected agent host. (medium confidence)

If backup processing cannot keep up before oplog history rolls over, backup can require resynchronization. Point-in-time recovery requires continuous oplog history; gaps can make a requested recovery point unusable. (low confidence)

If a source backup uses KMIP-based encryption at rest, the restore target needs access to the same KMIP server. The database can fail to start after restoration when that server is unavailable. (low confidence)

Do not classify every incomplete snapshot or frequent agent connection as a failure. A snapshot with complete:false may still be running, and short-lived automation connections are routine state checks. (medium confidence)

Backup sizing guidance treats 2 TB per replica set or shard as a planning recommendation rather than an Ops Manager limit. Resource consumption and recovery objectives require capacity planning rather than treating that number as a hard failure threshold. (medium confidence)
A Cloud Manager automation change can stall with open /data/db/mongod.lock: permission denied. The agent user needs ownership and read/write access to the database and log paths. (low confidence)

A September 2023 practitioner report describes SSL peer certificate validation failed: self signed certificate after enabling Cloud Manager TLS. The thread has no resolution; it demonstrates a client validation symptom, not a proven Cloud Manager defect or an established certificate fix. (low confidence)

An automated restore of only one shard fails; Ops Manager requires restoring all shards. Restored encrypted data also requires the target to reach the same KMIP server, otherwise mongod fails to start. (low confidence)

IBM Software Hub 5.2.x documents Ops Manager backups as disabled by default in its integration. A deployed or Running Ops Manager resource therefore does not by itself prove backups are configured; the integration requires configuring backup stores and explicitly enabling backup. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

A published third-party storage-backup experiment waits for the Ops Manager snapshot job to reach READY before taking array snapshots, catalogs complete sets, then checks restored document counts against captured baselines. This provides a concrete validation pattern; its demonstrated restore time is not a general Ops Manager RTO guarantee. (low confidence)
An automated sharded-cluster restore must restore all shards; attempting to restore one shard in isolation fails. (high confidence)

A reproduced third-party backup lab using Ops Manager demonstrates that dropping a database propagates through replica-set members. Replication therefore does not protect against that logical deletion; recovery requires a usable earlier backup. (low confidence)
